source.title: Llama-Mimi: Speech Language Models with Interleaved Semantic and Acoustic Tokens
source.authors: Issa Sugiura; Shuhei Kurita; Yusuke Oda; Ryuichiro Higashinaka

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether downstream speech-task performance changes with model size, using evaluation metrics rather than held-out pretraining loss or the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The model-size ablation reports five downstream metrics for 1.3B and 8B models. The semantic-token-weight and quantizer ablations, architecture comparison, and comparisons with other systems do not test the listed scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: This is a speech-LM architecture paper. Its only scale result compares two sizes (1.3B, 8B) on downstream speech metrics. There is no loss curve, no fit and no prediction, so it cannot show whether improvement is predictable (V6) or follows a power law (V5). The two sizes also come from different pretrained text backbones (Llama-3.2-1B vs Llama-3.1-8B), which confounds size. Kaplan et al. appears only as a citation supporting simple scalable decoders.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as a paraphrase of the model-size ablation. The paper's main conclusion, however, is that the flattened Llama-Mimi beats a hierarchical CSM counterpart on most tasks. It also finds a trade-off: weaker linguistic performance than phonetic-token models. Scaling is a minor ablation.
record.recipe_differences: Speech-model size ablation with downstream speech and linguistic evaluations; it does not fit held-out loss scaling laws or compute-optimal allocations.

fits_no_version.finding: In a flattened RVQ speech LM, moving from 1.3B to 8B (with different Llama backbones) raises all five downstream metrics. Gains are negligible on sWUGGY and speaker similarity and large on judged content quality (3.01 to 4.03).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger backbones improve downstream speech-continuation quality in flattened codec speech LMs (two-point, unfitted evidence).

record.problems: The size comparison uses only 1.3B and 8B models and reports no uncertainty estimates; it does not test a fitted scaling law or predict outcomes at larger sizes.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to the tested version were left out.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
The flattened vs hierarchical comparison is a different modelling scheme, not a depth/width shape sweep at fixed parameter count.
Speech modality, but no power-law form is fitted or tested.
Only two sizes, with no predictive relationship to scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'supports' label was inconsistent with its own 'partial' row states. With only two sizes, a confounded backbone, no uncertainty and no fit, predictability cannot be assessed, so no verdict is given. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit or prediction of larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token trend.
The architecture comparison is not a test of loss at fixed parameter count across depth, width, or other architecture details.
The study trains speech models but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in speech or other modalities or training regimes.
Tests downstream metric changes between only 1.3B and 8B; does not test prediction from pretraining loss or establish a fitted scaling relationship.
No comparison of fitting choices, exponents, or departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: Llama-Mimi-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared model-size ablation performance with Llama-Mimi-1.3B, keeping other training settings identical.
rows.note: The increase is small; the study reports consistent improvement across all listed tasks.
rows.check: Two-point size ablation with no fitted relationship; it cannot show predictable improvement. The change (68.7 to 68.8) is negligible. Size is confounded with a different pretrained backbone checkpoint.
